title: Pairing request response carries daemon-owned operator-channel truth
description: Dependency leaf carved from task-ea0106d. Enrich only the daemon pairing-handshake response contract: the core approval window continues to mint only requestId/confirmationLabel, while createPairingApprovalHandshake binds the daemon-owned `operatorChannel` availability fact into the public request result. This leaf does not thread process stdin yet; its immediate consumer is the daemon/listener composition child.
definitionOfDone: Re-measure pairing-approval-handshake.ts/.test.ts and exact-path porcelain before edits; verify no other live task owns the proposed response-contract hunk.

The successful pairing request result has exactly confirmationLabel, ok, operatorChannel, and requestId; operatorChannel is the exact constructor-supplied daemon fact for both true and false arms, while PairingRequestCreated/window state remains the existing three-key authority shape.
Claim behavior and every existing refusal preserve their exact code and CONTROL_ROOM_PAIRING_APPROVAL layer; no label, request id, credential, token, URL, or argv logging is added.
TDD and mutation drills prove flipping/omitting operatorChannel and widening either exact-key roster reds the named nonzero handshake assertions.
Daemon focused typecheck/test gates run standalone with exit 0 and nonzero counts; path-attributed broad red introduces no failure on the two owned paths.
taskRails: Do not put operator-channel state into PairingApprovalWindow or infer it from pairing availability; it is a daemon process fact supplied explicitly.
No secret-bearing pairing identity may enter logs, argv, URLs, refusal detail, or test transcripts.
reopenReason: Plan-time exploration found a clean-checkout wire break: adding an enumerable body key before the exact-key browser client lands makes all current pairing fail. Superseding with an additive response-header slice.
